The candidate evidence from people.json provides the canonical name 王隱. The annotation explicitly attributes the biographical note to 王隱's 晉書, confirming his role as the author. The reference semantics correctly notes that 王隱 is distinct from 張華 (the subject of the annotation).

The hard veto on c0 (explicit_identity_contradiction) is appropriate since 司空 here refers to 張華, not to a different person.

assertions.interpretation: The scene takes place on the wax (腊) festival day, when Hua Xin gathered his nephews and children for a banquet.
Wang Lang also imitated Hua Xin's practice of gathering family on the wax day, contemporaneous with the scene.
Someone later told Zhang Hua about this matter, occurring after the wax-day event itself.
Wang Lang was a native of Tan in Donghai and served as Situ (Minister over the Masses) under Wei, providing his identity and office context.
The Yiqishi clan first instituted the wax festival, an ancient origin background for the festival.

assertions.exact_span: 漢已來臘之明日為祝嵗古之遺語也
assertions.interpretation: Since the Han dynasty, the day after la was celebrated as 'zhusui', an ancient surviving custom, providing historical background on festival practices.
assertions.surface: 漢已來臘之明日為祝嵗古之遺語也

assertions.interpretation: Zhang Hua was successively promoted to Sikong (Minister of Works), providing his career/office context.

assertion.interpretation: Hua Xin on this occasion gathered his nephews and children for a drinking banquet, marking the event of the scene.
Wang Lang habitually (每) deferred to Hua Xin for his insight and bearing, a recurring background disposition preceding the specific wax-day event.

assertion.exact_span: 張曰王之學華皆是形骸之外去之所以更逺
assertion.interpretation: Zhang Hua's comment that Wang's imitation of Hua was only external form and thus farther from the essence, made at the later time when the matter was reported to him.
assertion.surface: 張曰王之學華皆是形骸之外去之所以更逺

assertion.exact_span: 三代名臘夏曰嘉平殷曰清祀周曰大蜡總謂之臘
assertion.interpretation: The annotation explains that across the Three Dynasties the wax festival had different names—Xia called it Jiaping, Yin Qingci, Zhou Da zha—all collectively called la, providing historical background on the festival.
assertion.surface: 三代名臘夏曰嘉平殷曰清祀周曰大蜡總謂之臘

assertion.exact_span: 嵗十二月合聚萬物而索饗之
assertion.interpretation: In the twelfth month of the year, all things are gathered and offered in sacrifice, describing the seasonal timing of the wax festival.
assertion.surface: 嵗十二月合聚萬物而索饗之

assertion.interpretation: Zhang Hua was later killed by Prince of Zhao, Lun, a later outcome of his life after the events of the story.
